questions.help:
Road traffic collisions  
   
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the enormous economic impact (either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs derived from road traffic accidents are classified as human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering. Material costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment. Healthcare costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations. Administrative costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.
(Página 248 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Safe driving  
   
2 Bends
If a vehicle enters into a bend at too high a speed, the tendency is for it to continue straight on, and not to go around the bend, this phenomenon is ‘centrifugal’ force. This means that when the road bends to the left, the vehicle will carry straight on, leaving the roadway on the right hand side.
When it is a right hand bend, the vehicle again continues straight but this time enters into a lane, where potentially traffic is coming in a head on direction, the vehicle also may potentially leave the road off the left side of the roadway.
(Página 223 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Head restraints are very effective in the event of a collision, avoiding or reducing the severity of injuries to the neck or vertebrates caused by the sudden movement, forward and back, of the head (whiplash). It is therefore imperative to properly use them, both in front and back seats.
Whiplash occurs when a person’s head moves backward and then forward suddenly with great force. It is particularly frequent in rear- ending collisions.
As well as muscle and head pain it can cause decreased neck mobility, vertigo or dizziness, among other symptoms.

17 Influence of drugs in road traffic collisions
The consumption of illegal drugs is related to many of the most serious accidents. A person driving under the influence of drugs puts all those around him/her at serious risk of accidents.
One of the effects of drugs is that risk perception decreases and some drugs can cause the driver to have an incorrect perception of time and space. The consumption of drugs will never improve reaction time. For people who take drugs and drive, the probability of having an accident is greater. It is forbidden to drive any vehicle with presence of drugs in the body. Substances excluded are those used under medical prescription and for therapeutic purposes, provided that the driver is able to manage the vehicle and drive with diligence, precaution and without distractions.
Driving with drugs present in the body may result in the loss of 6 points.

2.4.5 B permit
With a B driving licence which is at least two years’ old, it is possible to drive, within the country, vehicles without trailers powered by alternative fuels for the transport of goods with a MAM above 3,500 kg but below 4,250 kg. This is provided that the mass above 3,500 kg is solely due to the propulsion system compared to the propulsion system of a vehicle with the same dimensions which is equipped with a standard internal combustion engine with spark or compression ignition, and provided that it does not increase the load capacity with regards to the same vehicle.

2 Safety rules M.S.M.
2.2 Signal: Advising and warning of the manoeuvre
Generally, these warnings are made using the visual optical signals on the vehicle. If for any reasons the lighting signals are defective, (or as a reinforcement to the illuminated, optical signal) an arm signal should be given.
Exceptionally, and only where permitted, an acoustic, audible signal may be used to make the warning.
(Página 182 del manual 'Learning to drive')

2 Safety rules M.S.M.
2.2 Signal: Advising and warning of the manoeuvre
The brake lights advise and warn that a vehicle is reducing speed and potentially coming to a stop (temporary or permanent). The corresponding arm sign that warns of the same, consists of the arm being extended and moved up and down, in short and fast movements.
If the intention is to stop or to park, then in addition to the brake light, the directional indicators will be used that correspond to the side where the vehicle is moving to and where it will be stopped.
(Página 183 del manual 'Learning to drive')
